heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro—built for professional visual content creation with precision, fidelity, and multimodal control.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-bleed orange-led hero with layered abstract shells instead of a standard split layout. Keep the composition premium and unexpected: headline block anchored on one side, while the opposite side shows stacked floating product cards, prompt-to-output frames, and a subtle waveform/cinematic strip. Add a logo-proof bar beneath the headline area for B2B credibility. Use a soft-shadow card system, orange accent CTAs, white/near-black contrast, and decorative grid/orb elements for depth. The hero should feel enterprise-grade and creative-studio inspired, not generic SaaS.

repetitionBreakers: Hero is full-bleed and dynamic with layered media
Trust uses a marquee logo strip immediately after hero
Products switch to alternating split-panel layouts
A technical capability band breaks the rhythm before pricing
Testimonials use a carousel instead of a grid
Form ends on a centered high-contrast conversion card
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image & Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Seedream 4.5 for high-quality AI image generation and Seedance 1.5 Pro for AI video generation with audio. Built for creative teams, brand marketers, and enterprise content workflows.

sections.backgroundTreatment: orange full-bleed gradient wash with floating abstract shapes, layered prompt/output cards, and a dark proof chip band
sections.designNote: Content-first dynamic hero that answers what it is, who it is for, and what to do next. Keep the headline large but controlled for wrapping. Use the supplied headline, but visually reinforce continuity with the ad message using a short support stack, one primary button only, and an immediate proof strip. CTA text must be exactly 'Get started' and full-width on mobile. This hero should feel premium and visually rich, but still readable at a glance.

Place trust immediately after hero because traffic is warm and proof type is logos. Use 3-6 recognisable logo marks in a continuous marquee on a dark band for strong contrast. If official logos are unavailable, use an understated 'trusted by' logo wall style with SVG marks and no testimonial quotes here.

Use two alternating product blocks, not a generic SaaS feature grid. First block should spotlight Seedream 4.5 with a visual-left, text-right split and a preview panel showing text-to-image, edit, and composition. Second block should flip the rhythm for Seedance 1.5 Pro with text-left, visual-right, using cinematic frames and audio waveform overlays. Because there are 5+ features in each section, compress details into a spotlight-plus-grid or accordion-like feature matrix rather than a long repetitive list. Keep the emphasis on the 1-2 features that drove the click: high-fidelity image generation and synchronized video/audio generation.

Use this as a credibility and decision-support band rather than a generic benefits section. Since no dedicated why-techjockey content is provided, repurpose it into a compact enterprise-readiness strip: enterprise-ready infrastructure, multimodal content creation, fast evaluation, and creative confidence. Keep it lighter and more editorial than the product sections so the page breathes.

Show two clear plan cards or a side-by-side comparison, with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro separated by use case. This is a decision moment, so make the layout structured and readable. Do not invent new CTA labels; the purchase action must still be 'Get started' if a CTA is surfaced. Keep visual hierarchy stronger on the video plan if price anchoring is important, but do not overcrowd the section.

Use a testimonial carousel because there are 4+ testimonials. Make the quotes concise, role-forward, and enterprise-credible. Alternate slide backgrounds or subtle card treatments to avoid visual monotony. Avoid a dense quote wall; this section should feel like social proof, not a review dump.

End with a high-contrast conversion card on the brand orange background. Since CTA aggression should be strong for warm traffic, make this the final decisive action and keep the message focused on seeing it in action. Button text must be exactly 'Get started' and the mobile CTA must be full-width. Keep the form simple and visually premium, with one dominant action and no competing secondary buttons.

Use only if additional logos or media marks are available; otherwise this can serve as a compact footer-adjacent credibility strip. Keep it minimal and dark to contrast with the orange closing CTA. Do not introduce a newsletter-style pattern.

blueprint.designPersonality: Confident, polished, and commercially credible. Feels like a premium creative AI marketplace page for serious teams: orange-led, logo-heavy, modular, interactive, and distinctly Techjockey rather than generic SaaS.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use layered abstract product shells rather than literal screenshots: floating image frames, timeline strips, prompt-to-output cards, audio waveform overlays, and cinematic preview tiles. Add a dominant logo proof band near the top using SVG logos for trust. If brand or product media is missing, build rich CSS-based visual hierarchy with orange-tinted panels, metric chips, and shadowed content cards.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long, so the hero must use a smaller but still bold size to preserve hierarchy and avoid awkward wrapping.

colours.colourReason: The palette is derived strictly from Techjockey brand colors: orange #ff6b00 as the signature action color, white for clean contrast, near-black for text depth, and soft grey for structure. This keeps the experience brand-true and distinct without introducing any unapproved generic palette.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width dark hero band with brand/logo placement above a left-aligned headline stack, short supporting bullets, and a simple single-column content flow on mobile; emphasis is on clear hierarchy over visual complexity.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Intro hero, then a form/lead-capture block, followed by stacked feature/product sections with repeated heading + description + benefit list structure; progressive disclosure through separate feature blocks rather than dense all-at-once content.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Utility-first content cards with plain surfaces, minimal ornament, and strong text hierarchy; if used, cards should feel informational rather than promotional, with modest padding and simple borders/shadow only when needed.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA appears as a single high-contrast action in the hero and again within feature sections; the pattern favors one dominant conversion action per section and avoids competing secondary CTAs.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern is present; replace with lead-gen or inquiry-oriented conversion architecture if needed.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not visible in the reference; assume a lightweight, utilitarian footer with standard corporate links and contact/legal information.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Logo mark in hero plus text-led sections; no dominant product imagery or media panels are shown. Media usage should stay secondary and supportive, not immersive.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked feature sections with a section label, headline, descriptive paragraph, then a list of capability bullets. Each product area should be self-contained, easy to scan, and separated by clear vertical spacing.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form block immediately after the hero, presented as a prominent conversion card with a section heading and compact field layout; hidden tracking fields indicate a funnel-oriented capture pattern.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, low-motion presentation with no visible animated transitions; interaction should prioritize clarity and conversion over motion.
designNotes: Use a corporate B2B landing structure with strong conversion focus.
Keep content vertically stacked and scannable.
Maintain high contrast in the hero and crisp typography throughout.
Use repeated section templates to support long-form content without overwhelming the user.

blueprint.additionalInstructions: PROOF STRATEGY: The visitor trusts logos most. Make this the dominant trust signal.

mustHaveMoments: Prominent logo strip or enterprise trust bar near the top
Clear hero positioning for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro with a single primary CTA
Separate feature blocks for image and video models to reduce cognitive load
Short proof-led testimonial cluster to reinforce credibility
Lead-focused conversion section after feature explanation
Pricing/inquiry cards framed as quote or demo request, not ecommerce checkout
avoidPatterns: Overly decorative hero visuals that compete with the message
Multiple competing CTAs in the hero
Dense feature lists without visual breathing room
Long explanatory paragraphs before credibility is established
Purchase-oriented language that implies self-serve checkout
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is best positioned as a high-intent demo/inquiry landing page for professionals evaluating advanced generative AI. The audience is solution-aware and needs confidence in quality, reliability, and enterprise readiness more than broad education. Because the instruction says visitors trust logos most, the trust architecture should be logos-first, with brand proof placed immediately near the hero and repeated before the conversion moment. A split hero works best because it can carry a strong product message while leaving room for proof and a clear CTA. The page should stay product-led in structure, but proof-led in persuasion, using concise capability sections for Seedream and Seedance, then moving into testimonials and inquiry prompts. Strong CTA pressure is appropriate since the goal is lead capture or demo booking rather than passive awareness.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
